executiveSummary:
Monthly actuals across the pack are reported through Jan 26. Some visuals (for example the rolling/quarterly ARR and NRR views) reflect earlier periods by design; this is normal cadence and should be read alongside the latest monthly actuals. Overall, the data shows strong top-line momentum with ARR at £9.7M and ARR growth at 67%, healthy unit economics (CAC ratio 0.56; LTV:CAC 6.8), and improving profitability in the latest month. The primary constraint remains retention, with logo and gross retention below typical SaaS benchmarks and a trailing NRR in the low 90s, albeit stabilising in recent months. Cost mix is trending in the right direction, supporting a path to sustained profitability.

  • Retention quality and durability: Logo retention (86%), gross retention (80%), and trailing NRR (~92% on the rolling view) indicate elevated downsell/attrition pockets. Typical response: cohort and root-cause analysis (product fit, usage, segment), targeted account reviews, and pricing/packaging guardrails to support GRR/NRR recovery.
  • New business engine efficiency: Last 3 months skew to new logo lands versus expansion, while CAC ratio (0.56) and payback indicators are attractive. Typical response: funnel diagnostics (source mix, win rates), capacity planning, and guardrails to preserve CAC/payback as volume scales.
  • Operating leverage and cost mix: Gross margin sits c.78% and the latest month EBIT turns positive on the P&L page, with S&M/Dev/G&A mix still material. Typical response: spend and hiring pacing reviews, margin improvement initiatives, and ongoing unit-economics tracking to maintain Rule of 40 performance.
page1:
The dashboard indicates £9.7M ARR with 67% growth and strong unit economics (CAC ratio 0.56; LTV:CAC 6.8). Gross and recurring margins (78% and 83%) are healthy for the model. Retention metrics are the principal drag: logo retention at 86%, gross retention at 80%, and net retention at 92% trail common SaaS benchmarks. The cost mix shows S&M at 36% of revenue, Development at 28%, and G&A at 20%, resulting in an EBIT margin of -6% on this view; the Rule of 40 registers at 61%, supported by growth. This page reflects a monthly dashboard view; it should be read together with the detailed monthly P&L (reported through Jan 26) on the dedicated page.

Management focus reinforced from the Executive Summary: retention quality and durability, and sustaining the efficiency of the new logo engine.
page2:
The ARR and deals page is reported monthly through Jan 26. January closed with ARR of £9,686k, a net increase of £270k. The month comprised £180k of new lands (2 new logos), £90k of expansion, and £45k of downsell with no recorded logo attrition. Logo count stands at 98. After volatility in late 2025 (notably weaker gross/net retention in Oct–Nov), recent months show improvement with Jan net % at 112%. Deal volumes remain variable month-on-month, consistent with an emerging but active pipeline.

Management focus reinforced: continue strengthening retention—carry forward the improved Jan net %—through account reviews in cohorts that showed prior weakness.
page3:
This P&L and headcount page is reported monthly through Jan 26. Revenue in Jan was £833k with gross margin of £650k (78%). Operating costs were £629k, yielding EBIT of £21k (2%), marking a month-on-month improvement from prior losses. Cost mix in Jan shows S&M £242k (29% of revenue), Development £242k (29%), and G&A £145k (17%). The CAC ratio printed 0.81 in Jan (variable by month, but supportive of payback). Headcount totals 65, up from earlier months, primarily in Development (30) with S&M stable at 21.

Management focus reinforced: operating leverage and cost mix—continue spend discipline and hiring pacing to maintain positive EBIT while protecting growth capacity.
page4:
This ARR page mixes cadences: the rolling quarterly view runs through Dec 25 and the NRR rolling line extends into early 2026, while the composition tables reconcile to the latest monthly ARR total of £9,686k. Concentration is diversified but led by Energy & Utilities (£3,994k) and Life Science (£2,498k); by region, South America (£2,318k) and Asia (£2,093k) are the largest. The 12‑month waterfall shows strong additions (£4,320k) and upsell (£709k) offset by downsell (£270k) and logo loss (£878k). The rolling NRR trends around the low 90s by early 2026, consistent with the retention gap seen on the dashboard.

Management focus reinforced: retention durability—cohort and segment analysis (by vertical/region) to prioritise interventions where losses and downsells concentrated in late 2025.
page5:
The last‑3‑months view covers Nov 25 to Jan 26. Total ARR movement was +£855k across 13 logos, with a mix skewed to new lands (£720k across 8 logos) over expansion (£180k) and limited downsell (‑£45k). Activity was broadly distributed by industry (notably Energy & Utilities and Government) and by region (South America and Africa each contributed materially to new ARR). Customer-level data confirms dispersion across multiple accounts rather than concentration in a single win.

No new management focus items identified on this page.
page6:
This budget analysis references the 2025 budget (Budget Month: Dec 25) and includes ARR v Budget through Jan 26. On an annual basis, EBITDA is £30k better than budget (5%), with revenue slightly ahead (~1%) and mixed cost variances (G&A favourable; S&M modestly over). Quarterly and monthly views both show positive EBITDA variances, indicating improving execution into the latest periods. ARR is tracking above budget: Annual ARR v Budget is +£382k (+11%), driven by stronger additions (+8%) and lower attrition (+12%) than planned, partially offset by softer upsell (‑6%) and higher downsell (‑9%). The ARR v Budget chart shows current ARR pacing marginally above plan into Jan 26.

No new management focus items identified on this page.
